processing: Registered as a sencha cultivar; also sold lightly shaded as kabusecha, which softens astringency and builds umami.
harvest_season: Early spring: it buds early, which makes it exposed to late frosts and better suited to warmer areas.
appearance_dry: Dark green rolled needles, as is typical of sencha and kabusecha.
appearance_liquor: Clear yellow-green, as is typical of sencha and kabusecha.
taste_profile: Pleasant umami and sweetness with refreshing green notes, at least in its kabusecha form.

brewing.notes: For kabusecha, go cooler and slower than for sencha. Raise the temperature with each steep.

vintage_note: As with other Japanese green teas, it is sold as the latest spring harvest and is best within about a year. It usually appears as a small single-cultivar lot, such as a Wazuka kabusecha, named by farm and region.
description:
Shunmei is an early-budding Japanese green tea cultivar, bred at a national experiment station in Shizuoka. It is uncommon on the shelf, and mostly known in the West through single-cultivar lots.

It was registered with sencha in mind, but one of the better-known examples outside Japan is a kabusecha from Wazuka in Kyoto. Light shading before picking moves the cup toward umami and away from astringency.

That Wazuka tea is described as savoury and sweet with a fresh green edge. Treat it gently, with water around 65°C for the first steep; boiling water will flatten the sweetness.

When buying, note that a pack may say kabusecha or sencha, and those are noticeably different cups from the same bush. If you like this, try other early cultivars from warmer districts.
history:
Shunmei was bred at Japan's Vegetable and Tea Experiment Station in Shizuoka and registered in 1988. Its parents are recorded as Yutakamidori and F1NN8, the latter descending from Tamamidori and Shizuoka Zairai No. 6.

The name is written 旬茗 and refers to seasonal, early tea, though explanations of its exact meaning differ.
